content:
The Grok Bot, under SpaceXAI, has sparked a consumer-facing AI agent app craze this summer. Facing competitors like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's ChatGPT Dot, the Grok Bot has just completed a new round of feature upgrades with the assistance of Anthropic's Claude.

The Grok Bot now uses Claude Opus 5.5 as its intelligence engine.

The Grok Bot officially launched in August, with dedicated apps released specifically for iPhone and iPad. The iPad version and more affordable subscription plans followed in September.

Entering October, the Grok Bot will receive a major backend upgrade, switching to Anthropic's Claude as its intelligence core, replacing the less impressive model previously provided by SpaceXAI/Cursor.

For background, Anthropic became a SpaceX customer this year, purchasing computing power from them to support Claude's operations.

From today onwards, the Grok Bot is able to use Claude Opus 5.5, which is the latest version of Anthropic's most powerful model.

The Grok Bot's current upgrade comes as Meta pushes its nearly free Muse agent (which recently also arrived on iPad), while OpenAI actively expands its proactively operating ChatGPT Dot powered by Astra.

The Grok Bot is now available simultaneously on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Have you used any of these AI agent systems yet?

Make the most of your Apple products' power.
